title: dev-pre-pr pre-pr.json — the branch readiness verdict
description: The output of the dev-pre-pr skill, written to <evid_root>/<key>/pre-pr.json. The last gate before infra-ship: it consolidates the loop's existing evidence (regression.json, review.json) with a deterministic standards scan and emits one verdict the recipe router branches on. The router reads `status`: ready|warnings advance to ship, blocked routes back to dev-fix (or escalates). `sources` is the anti-stale-evidence record — every check names where its answer came from, so a PASS can always be dated against the diff.

status.description: ready = validations pass with no blockers and no warnings; warnings = passes with non-blocking findings (still advances — a MEDIUM that cannot block must not spin the loop); blocked = a blocker, or evidence that could not be established at all (fail closed).

next_action.description: escalate rather than re-fix when re-fixing cannot help: the scan could not run, the repo is in a bad state, or the same blocker already survived a fix cycle.

base.description: The base the diff was taken against — the merge-base, not the base tip.

checks.description: One entry per validation. The build/lint/tests gates are keyed per layer (frontend_*, backend_*): a stack with one project uses the pair that fits and marks the other `skipped`; a stack with more projects (conventions.projects[]) may add `<project>_build|lint|tests` keys with the same enum. `skipped` is a legitimate result when the layer was not touched; it is NOT a pass.

fix_verified.description: v1.1.0. Did qa-verify prove the fix works? Read from verify.json.verdict. ANY value other than `pass` or `not-applicable` is a BLOCKER at every tier — this is the mechanical form of the 'fix verification always runs' invariant, which until v1.1.0 was enforced only by the recipe advancing stage-by-stage. `missing` = no verify.json; `malformed` = present but unreadable or contract-invalid; `not-applicable` = this run legitimately has no fix to verify (a docs-only branch, or a standalone developer pre-pr check outside any loop). `not-applicable` is the ONLY non-pass value that does not block, and a loop run may never use it.

sources.description: Provenance + freshness for each adopted answer — the anti-stale-evidence record. `stale` means the artifact predates a changed source file and was therefore re-run rather than trusted.

verify.description: v1.1.0. Freshness of verify.json, judged the same way as regression: stale = a changed source file is newer than the artifact. Unlike regression, a STALE verify may NOT be re-run by this skill — dev-pre-pr has no Edit tool and cannot drive a browser, and a verify it could run itself would not be blind. Stale therefore routes to re-fix (re-verify), it does not degrade to ran-locally.

violations.description: Every standards finding, blocking or not — the scanner's output plus the reader-judged (Half 2) rules, in one shape. `heuristic: true` findings NEVER block unless `confirmed: true`.

fix.description: What to do instead — the half a developer actually reads.

confirmed.description: A heuristic that was read and upheld. Only a confirmed heuristic may block.

source.description: standards_check = the deterministic scanner (scripts/standards_check.sh over the conventions.json rules); reader = a finding the gate confirmed by reading the file; review.json = adopted from dev-code-review; task.md = an open item rolled up from the branch's review-notes file.

blockers.description: The things that must change before a human should see this as a PR. Empty on ready/warnings.

warnings.description: Real but non-blocking: medium/low violations, unconfirmed heuristics, a skipped review stage.

confirmed_clear.description: Heuristics that were read and cleared — recorded so the next run does not re-litigate them.

summary.description: Why this verdict, in a sentence a developer can act on.

attempt.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2.0). Which attempt of this stage produced the artifact, 1-based. Added because the retry audit had to be reconstructed from session transcripts — no artifact recorded its own attempt number, so a retry was indistinguishable from a first pass after the fact. A retry requires transient-failure evidence; a deterministic failure escalates or changes strategy instead of repeating.

retry_reason.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2.0). Why this attempt happened, when attempt > 1 — the flaky-store match, infra error, timeout or oracle exit 2 that justified it.

timing.description: OPTIONAL (v1.2.0). When this stage ran. Costs microseconds to write and is the only way to tell whether a pipeline redesign still holds months later — without it every duration has to be reconstructed from session transcripts, which do not always exist.
